shots.line: In this town, everyone bet on Kalshi to get rich. Nikhil put the odds of a snow day on our school lawn.
Prakhar bet the fountain would turn gold. One second it was water. The next, coins rained down on his head.
Then my phone lit up in my bedroom. Will Khai disappear by midnight? I had ninety-nine percent odds of vanishing.
I showed Leo at the diner. He snatched my phone and flipped it over. Last week, they bet I'd lose my voice, he whispered.
At town hall, Mayor Michael slid a contract across his desk. A million dollars if nobody could say my name after midnight. Anyone who bet yes would forget me.
Outside, my dad Kyle was selling tickets to watch me disappear. He saw me wave and turned the sign so I could read it. Admission, five dollars.
I ran to the only empty betting booth. One dollar left. I dropped it in and slammed No.
At midnight the streetlights went out. I stood right in front of Leo, but he looked straight through me.
Then Leo grabbed my sleeve. Khai! He'd never placed a bet. The board flashed No. Dad remembered me and tore up his tickets.
We climbed onto the roof. My phone buzzed. Will Khai tell anyone? I hit record and told the whole town. That one settled yes before they could even bet.
